title: How screening participation has been increased elsewhere

items.text: In a randomised trial in Espoo, mailing an HPV self-sampling kit to women who had missed screening brought in more participants than a reminder letter (29.8% vs 26.2%).

sources.title: Virtanen et al. 2011, International Journal of Cancer

items.text: Offering self-sampling as the first reminder raised total attendance by 17%. A cost analysis suggests a letter as the first reminder and self-sampling as the second.

sources.title: Virtanen, Anttila & Nieminen 2015, BMC Women's Health

items.text: An opt-in model, where non-attenders order a self-sampling kit on request, was also found feasible in Finland.
Stockholm sent self-sampling kits directly to about 330,000 women instead of an invitation. Organised screening test coverage rose from 54% to 60% within a year.
A systematic review found that postal and telephone reminders, a GP signature on the invitation, and a pre-booked appointment (instead of an open invitation) increase participation.
In colorectal screening, advance notification letters, mailing the faecal test home, written reminders and a phone call from an adviser increase test return.

sources.title: Rat et al. 2018, European Journal of Cancer Prevention (systematic review)

items.text: Pre-screening reminders, GP endorsement, more personal reminders and more acceptable tests (e.g. self-sampling) also work in under-served groups.
